shape_hint: Low hexagon nut (height about half the thread diameter) with a 30 degree chamfer on both faces (style 0); side view is a short hexagon prism of height m, top view a hexagon with width across flats s and across corners e; countersink of diameter da at the thread ends.
notes: Kept: pitch, s, e_min, m (max) and m_min for all 19 candidate sizes M3-M48, each cell with 3 to 6 clusters out of globalfastener, amesweb, fasten.it, engineersedge, schrauben-lexikon and nfgab. Choice of rectangle: the nominally largest one is 12 sizes x 8 columns (96 cells: M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, M10, M12, M14, M18, M22, M27, M33 with s_min, dw_min, da_max added) because engineersedge - the third cluster for those tolerance columns - lists only M1.6-M12 and the non-preferred sizes; 19 sizes x 5 columns (95 cells) is kept instead so that M16, M20, M24, M30, M36, M42 and M48 stay in the table. NOT counted: (1) boltport's ISO 4035 page, because it reproduces the standard's scope paragraph, requirements table and normative references (SOURCE_RULE: such pages are not sources); (2) fasteners.eu's 'ISO 4035' page and its torqbolt copy, because the table printed there is the DIN 439-2 table (M1,8, fine-thread designations, s 17/19/22/32, m' row, e M5 9.79). If fasteners.eu is counted where it agrees (as was done for pws), s_min, dw_min and da_max also reach three clusters for M16, M20, M24, M36, M42 and the largest rectangle becomes 17 sizes x 8 columns (or 19 sizes x 7 columns without dw_min): run `python3 -I hnthin_compare.py --count-fe` -> hnthin.alt_fe.json. EDITION CAVEAT for the columns left out: every page read gives the rounded one-decimal numbers of the 1999/2012 editions for mw_min, dw_min and da_max (e.g. M6 mw 2.3, dw 8.9; M12 da 13.0); no public HTML page carries two-decimal numbers such as dw 8.88 or da 12.96 (globalfastener lists an ISO 4035-2023 entry but serves no table for it), so the catalog's present two-decimal values in those three columns could not be confirmed by any fetched page. nfgab's page 'ISO 4035/DIN 439' says itself that M10, M12, M14 and M22 are listed with DIN widths; it dissents there and agrees elsewhere. boltport's pitch column ('pa'), engineersedge's m' and schrauben-lexikon's 'm' (no max/min) and 'd2' rows were not used because the pages do not state what they are.

verification.checks_done: Verifier re-fetched every page itself on 2026-11-11 with curl (browser UA, 2.5 s pause per host; HTTP 200 for all; globalfastener detail_400 needed one retry after a 403), wrote its own stdlib HTML table reader (vt.py, gf.py, obs.py) and counting script (count.py) without using the researcher's raw/, extracted tables or scripts. Drawings that define bare symbols (schrauben-lexikon gifs, nfgab pngs) were fetched and viewed. Lead decisions applied: amesweb (calculator) not a source; a rival value printed by 2+ independent lineages removes the row; cells of another standard printed under the target title (verified equal to that standard's table) are neither support nor rival; pages reproducing the standard's text (boltport ISO 4035) excluded. A cluster whose own pages give two different values for a cell is not counted for it. Largest rectangle (cells, then rows) chosen among column subsets that contain the drawing keys. Re-counted 19 x 5 candidate cells; kept 11 x 5; per-cell clusters in hnthin.verify.md. | Lead chose the verifier's stated alternative rectangle: 17 sizes (M3–M42 without M14) × s, e_min, m — every cell ≥3 independent clusters, no rival (hnthin.verify.md). pitch and m_min dropped (2 clusters without the calculator); M14 (rival e min 23.35 on two pages) and M48 dropped.
